reviewed_by: Claude review of alias targets missing from the account model catalog
reason: #380 resolves an OpenRouter alias through `alias_target` before endpoint discovery, but the deploy showed the field never arrives: Nebula discovers models from `/v1/models/user` (catalog_source `openrouter:/models/user`), and that payload has no `alias_target` key at all - the live account catalog returned all 17 `~author/family-latest` entries with `alias_target: null`, while the public `/v1/models` catalog carries `{"alias_target": {"slug": "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"}}` for the same id. Without the field, discovery still queried the alias, still got an empty endpoint set, and the 8,192-token ceiling stayed. A health refresh now fills that one field from the public catalog when the account catalog contains an alias, reusing the existing paged fetch (extracted as `_openrouter_public_catalog`, which `_openrouter_models_served_by` now shares). The selection runs test_providers for the new health behaviour and the paging refactor, and the other three descriptor suites because they consume the descriptors this path produces.
exclusions: No frontend unit tests: ui/src is untouched and no new field reaches the wire types the UI maps. No native tests: no Tauri or catalog-code change. No screenshot baselines: no rendered surface changes. No Playwright: the behaviour depends on the live OpenRouter account and public catalogs, which the Playwright stubs do not model; the mocked and real-Core journeys assert provider selection, not catalog enrichment. tests/test_playwright_impact.py is excluded because ui/playwright-impact.json is unchanged. No full suites.
